newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma urges ASEAN to resist U.S. pressure.
newsitem.headline: Burma urges ASEAN to resist U.S. pressure.

text.p: Burma on Saturday urged its neighbours to resist pressure by the United States aimed at preventing Rangoon's entry into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year.

"ASEAN will have to stick to its guns to show that nobody dictates to us," a government official told Reuters in a telephone interview. "Generally we believe if ASEAN gives in this time then ASEAN will have to give in every time."

He was responding to remarks made in Washington on Friday by U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, who said the United States was lobbying members of ASEAN not to admit Burma to the seven-member regional grouping this year.

"We don't believe that ASEAN should take this step," Burns said. "We're trying to use our influence with the ASEAN partners to make the point that Burma should be given a stiff message that it's not welcome. I have no idea at this point what action ASEAN will take."

The comment by Burns appeared to step up Western unhappiness about the plan to admit Burma, where Washington banned new U.S. investment on Tuesday as condemnation of the military regime's human rights abuses and its repression of the democracy movement led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
The Burmese official said he was not surprised the U.S. was lobbying ASEAN.
"I knew of course that they were going to try to increase the pressure," the government official said. "We have said they would put more and more pressure on Myanmar (Burma)."
"ASEAN countries have seen through the pretext the United States has been using. They have realised it's not democracy the United States wants to impose here, it's hypocrisy," he said.

Last week the leaders of ASEAN -- which comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- said the U.S. economic sanctions would not affect Burma's admission to the regional grouping.
ASEAN had been expected to admit Burma, along with Cambodia and Laos, later this year.
